name: Okra Root-Knot Nematode
description: A soil-borne nematode pest that causes galls on okra roots, impairing water and nutrient uptake. It is a significant problem in sandy soils and continuous okra production areas of Nigeria.
symptoms: Galls or knots on roots visible upon uprooting
Stunted plant growth and wilting during dry periods
Yellowing of leaves and nutrient deficiency symptoms
Plants appear stressed even with adequate water
causes: Sandy or loamy soils with good aeration
Introduction through infected seedlings or tools
treatments: Apply organic amendments (neem cake, poultry manure) to suppress nematodes
Use carbofuran or nematicides in severe infestations
Solarize soil during hot dry season before planting
prevention: Practice crop rotation with marigold or grasses
Incorporate neem cake or organic matter into soil before planting
Use disease-free nursery beds and clean tools
Avoid moving infested soil between fields
